16.0.s.en: (1) The women's visit to the tomb

16.0.0.en: "When the sabbath was past": that is, after sunset, the women bought spices to go with them to the tomb to complete the wrapping of the body of the Lord Jesus. This is a new proof of the intensity of their love for Christ on the one hand, and on the other that the idea of the Lord's resurrection was completely far from their minds.

16.0.1.en: Note: Christ spent in the tomb part of Friday, and also the night of the Sabbath and its day, and then the night of Sunday until its dawn. By the reckoning followed among the Jews, the period is counted as three days.

16.1.0.en: "Very early": this expression agrees with the words of John the Evangelist in (20:1), "early, when it was yet dark," yet St. Mark adds "at the rising of the sun," and so we understand that the women's departure from the city was while it was still dark. And when they arrived, the features of the day were becoming clear, and their thought was occupied with whom they would find to roll away for them the very great stone, which needed several men to remove it.

16.2.0.en: When they arrived, a surprise awaited them, for they found that the stone had been moved from its place and the tomb was open. And when they entered, they found an angel in white garments, who appeared to them in the form of a man, and they were amazed. St. Luke indicates (24:4), "behold, two men stood by them," and St. John indicates (20:12) "two angels in white." And as happens when each witness of an event sheds light on certain different aspects of that event, it is most likely that Mark mentioned only the angel who spoke.

16.3.0.en: The angel hastened to speak to them, reassuring them not to be afraid or amazed, for he knew whom they sought. "Jesus of Nazareth, which was crucified": it would have sufficed the angel to say Jesus, or the Nazarene, or the Crucified, but he said the name of the Lord and His attributes to assure them that he was speaking of the same Person without any confusion.

16.3.1.en: "Crucified": he could have said the Risen One instead of the Crucified, but the Crucified is the attribute of love, self-giving and redemption, and it became a title that does not leave Christ even after His resurrection, and a pride to all of us, and a emblem of our acceptance of His love and His boundless redemption.

16.3.2.en: "Behold the place": the angel pointed to the place where the body of the Saviour had been laid to confirm the emptiness of the place and the resurrection of Christ.

16.3.3.en: God fulfilled His promise of the resurrection ... and therefore we must trust that He is faithful and true, fulfilling all His promises, for the power of God that raised the body of Christ from the dead is available to us to raise our souls, dead morally and spiritually, to life, so that we can change and grow and live the life of the resurrection.

16.4.0.en: The angel asked the women to go and tell the disciples and Peter the news of the resurrection and its confirmation, and that they should go to Galilee, where Christ would go before them and appear to them as confirmation of His resurrection from the dead. But the disciples were filled with terror, so they remained in Jerusalem (Jn 20:19, 26), and the Lord Jesus met them first in Jerusalem (Lk 24), and afterward in Galilee (Jn 21), then returned to Jerusalem, where He ascended to heaven from the Mount of Olives (Acts 1:2).

16.4.1.en: And we learn from this something for ourselves, that it is not enough for every Christian to profess his faith, but he must also inform others of the salvation and the lasting acceptance by Christ, whatever their sins may be, and this the Church teaches us in the Divine Liturgy when we all sing the hymn: "Amen ... Amen ... Amen, we proclaim Your death, O Lord, and we confess Your holy resurrection and Your ascension into the heavens."

16.5.0.en: St. Mark explains here the feelings of the women who visited the tomb, for in spite of the angel's words and his encouragement of them, human weakness, together with the greatness of the event, caused feelings of fear and bewilderment to take hold of them.

16.5.1.en: "Neither said they any thing to any man": St. Luke tells us (24:9) that they "returned from the sepulchre, and told all these things unto the eleven, and to all the rest," and consequently we understand that they told no one on the way back, not even friends, except the disciples first.

16.6.s.en: (2) The appearance to Magdalene and two disciples, then to the rest of the disciples

16.6.0.en: Matthew and Luke, together with Mark, mention that Mary Magdalene was among the first women who went to the tomb, whether she was with the other Mary (Mt 28:1), or with other women as Luke mentioned (24:10), and John mentioned that she was alone on one occasion (20:1, 2, 11-17). The meaning is that she was the common factor in more than one visit. And the motive driving her was the deep love for the person of the Lord Jesus, and for this she deserved to see Him with Mary and then another time alone, and she went to inform the disciples, who, because of their grief and the intensity of their emotion, did not believe. And what Mark did not mention is that Peter and John went in haste to investigate the matter (Jn 20:4-10).

16.6.1.en: "Seven devils": St. Luke also mentioned this (8:2) without detail. But what concerns us here is that God is able to defeat all the forces of evil in a person however great they are (seven being one of the numbers of perfection), on condition that the person humbles himself and lets God work ... Amen.

16.7.0.en: Another appearance that St. Mark mentions here is His appearance to two of His disciples (of the seventy apostles). Though Mark mentioned it briefly, Luke related it in detail, and they were known as the disciples of Emmaus (24:13-35), and it is mentioned that they are the two disciples whom, when they told the eleven, the eleven did not believe, but doubted their account.

16.7.1.en: Here, when the two disciples of Emmaus recognized Christ, they returned to tell the disciples ... so what do we do, having known that Christ is God manifested in the flesh and seeing Him in His repeated visits to us ... do we hold fast to Him, and call people to meet Him in His Church and enjoy the taste of His most holy Body?!

16.8.0.en: "Afterward he appeared": the word "afterward" here does not mean the last visit or appearance of Christ among His disciples, but means after the last two appearances that he mentioned (to Mary and to the disciples of Emmaus), for He appeared to the eleven as they sat together, and rebuked them strongly for not believing what they had heard from others about the news of His resurrection.

16.8.1.en: St. Mark took care to bring out the essence of Christ's message to the disciples as he concludes his Gospel, and for this reason he did not mention whether this appearance was in Jerusalem or in Galilee, but also in his brevity he suggests to the reader that Christ's appearance to His disciples after the resurrection and His ascension to the heavens are one scene (v. 19), but of course this did not happen so, rather he mentioned it for the sake of brevity and summary and concern for the substance, as we mentioned.

16.9.0.en: As for the substance of the message to the disciples, it is the preaching of the Kingdom of God, and the redemption of the whole world by Christ and the salvation of everyone who believes in Him. And the two expressions "all the world" and "every creature" mean the commissioning of the Church with what the pure Apostles began of preaching, for how many millions are still far from the salvation of Christ and have not heard of it, and how many souls, after hearing, turned back and drew far from the essence of the spiritual life ... so Christ's commission to us is clear, and the work needs great divine help, with the present world turning to evil.

16.10.0.en: This is the only and first entrance to salvation, faith in the name of Christ and then holy Baptism, and this is what the Church has done through time in her preaching, for she delivers the faith and then gathers the believers who received the faith and baptizes them in the name of the most holy Trinity at the hands of the Apostles, bishops and priests. And because of the importance of this sacrament and its standing in the Church, the Church does not accept any joining her and sharing in the rest of the sacraments except by Baptism. And the Church rejects the strange teaching that Baptism is merely a sign, for the word of the Lord Christ is clear that whoever heard and did not believe and was not baptized became condemned before God. And in our present time the child is baptized on the faith of his parents, and from here the parents are responsible before God for planting faith in the hearts of their children.

16.11.0.en: With the commission to preach to the whole world and every creature, the Lord Christ gave encouragement to the pure Apostles that miracles would accompany them as necessary proofs for unbelievers in that time, and likewise their speaking in languages they had not known before for the spreading of the preaching.

16.11.1.en: "They shall take up serpents": what is meant by this expression is that serpents will not harm them, which is also what the Lord had said earlier to the disciples: "Behold, I give unto you power to tread on serpents and scorpions" (Lk 10:19). We may see this happen with the children of God, as happened with St. Paul in a miraculous way when he shook the serpent off (Acts 28:4-5). And the other, more distant meaning is that serpents signify the evil surrounding man, which he cannot face except by a special power that God gives to His children, and they obtain it through their complete dependence on Him and their perseverance in prayer.

16.12.0.en: After many appearances and teaching, St. Mark mentions the ascension of the Lord Jesus Christ to the heavens (see Acts 1:9).

16.12.1.en: "On the right hand of God": a figurative expression meaning glory, majesty and power, that is, that Christ returned to His glory that He had hidden from us in the time of His Incarnation.

16.13.0.en: St. Mark ends his Gospel with a verse that expresses the work of the Church extending from the age of the Apostles to this day of ours, which is going out to preach in the name of Christ, and just as the pure Apostles experienced the work of the Lord with them, the Church – in the person of her servants, her priests and her bishops – still experiences the strong hand of God working in the ministry and in drawing souls to the true faith.

16.13.1.en: Grant me, O Lord, to be a fruitful branch in Your vine, and a preaching member of Your Kingdom, steadfast in Your Church and Your word, so that I may first be satisfied ... and draw my brethren to You for Your glory alone ... Amen.
